item.title: Snow expected as cold snap on the way
item.description: Start wrapping up, as a cold snap is on the way, according to Met Éireann. Temperatures are expected to dip as a polar air mass moves over the country from Friday. Wintry showers, freezing fog and snow is expected in some areas. Advertisement Martin Matthews forecaster with Met Eireann has more: Advertisement

item.title: Pharmacy and three apartments planned for Ballinamore
item.description: Plans have been lodged for a new pharmacy and three apartments in Ballinamore. They'd be located in High Street. Two of the apartments would have one bedroom, and the other would have two bedrooms. Advertisement Bryan Cribbin is looking for planning permission from Leitrim County Council, who are due to make a decision at the end of February.

item.title: Don't use 'garage heaters' in houses - Leitrim Fire Service
item.description: Leitrim Fire Service is warning people of the danger of using outdoor heaters in houses over the festive period. They're issuing advice to prevent the usual increase in domestic blazes at this time of the year. Martin Bond is the senior assistant chief fire officer - he says he's concerned about 'alternative heating devices': Advertisement

item.title: Staff for big Longford employers struggle to find homes
item.description: Major employers say there's a growing demand among workers for housing in Longford. It follows a major funding announcement earlier this month for the construction of 25 new affordable homes in the county. The Department of Housing says the €1.8 million project will be carried out at Ard Micheal on the Ballinalee Road. item.title: 22 people stranded on trolleys in Sligo hospital
item.description: A total of 22 people are languishing on trolleys in Sligo University Hospital today. It's one of the most overcrowded hospitals in the country. Nationally, there are 190 admitted patients waiting for beds today. Advertisement That's a long way off the record high - of over 900 - but the figure tends to rise from early January.

item.title: 20,000 people admitted to two local hospitals on trolleys in 2025
item.description: Almost 20,000 people were admitted to two local hospitals on trolleys this year. That includes over 11,600 in University Hospital Galway, and over 8,000 in Sligo University Hospital. The figure was 4,340 in Castlebar hospital, 1,360 in Mullingar, 1,157 in Portiuncula in Ballinasloe - but only 73 in Tullamore. item.title: Challenge people if they're drunk behind wheel - gardai
item.description: Gardai have appealed to people to prevent drink and drug-drivers getting behind the wheel during the busy New Year period. Roads around the country are expected to be particularly busy tonight and tomorrow. Almost 600 people have been arrested for being under the influence of cocaine, cannabis or alcohol in the month of December alone. item.title: Strict visitor restrictions imposed in Tullamore hospital
item.description: Visiting has been restricted in all wards in Tullamore hospital due to a spike in people admitted with winter illnesses. The Midland Regional Hospital says it's experiencing a high number of people with respiratory viral illness, such as flu and the winter-vomiting bug. Hospital bosses said: "As a precautionary measure,visiting restrictions have been implemented across all hospital departments to help reduce the spread of the virus within the healthcare setting. item.title: €33,000 worth of cocaine and cannabis seized in Boyle
item.description: A man has been charged after a major seizure of cannabis and cocaine in north Roscommon. Gardaí on patrol at Corrigeenroe, Boyle, stopped and searched a vehicle at around 1 o'clock yesterday morning and recovered cannabis herb, cannabis resin and cocaine with an estimated street value of more than €33,000.
